why_relevant: Ranking/profile site for the largest MK companies; sizes integrators (revenue, employees) so supplier tiers can be ranked before deeper tracking.

source_name: Thales CPL partner directory (Nextsense DOO entry)
why_relevant: Global-vendor partner directories are a reliable, structured way to identify which MK local firms are authorised channel partners for HSM/card/identity technology used by banks.

Swiss group with a large Skopje engineering entity (registered 2001) whose payments arm builds 3-D Secure and digital-payment products; MK operation is a major local employer and payments-capability pool.

source_name: NBRSM — Payment institutions, e-money institutions and payment system operators (hub page)
why_relevant: Central hub of the licensed non-bank payments layer created by the 2022 Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems; from here the individual public registers (PI, EMI, PSO, AISP, agents/branches) branch off. This is the master actor-list for the cell: every licensed PSP/EMI is a potential procurer of switch, POS, KYC and processing technology.

source_name: NBRSM — Register of electronic money institutions (Регистар на институции за електронски пари)
why_relevant: Authoritative list of licensed EMIs (e.g. Paysera Macedonia, Flex Pay reported as licensees). Each new entry is a newly funded buyer that must procure a core wallet/ledger platform, KYC/AML tooling, card issuing and processing — the leading indicator for this cell's demand.

source_name: NBRSM — Licensing procedures for PI/EMI (Издавање дозволи)
why_relevant: Sets out application requirements, fees and the licensing contact (licenciranjepups@nbrm.mk). Requirements dictate what technology an applicant must have in place before licensing (security, safeguarding accounts, incident reporting) — i.e. it defines the mandatory procurement basket for every new PSP.

source_name: NBRSM — Decision on issuing licences/approvals to PI and EMI and on keeping the registers
why_relevant: The bylaw that defines the exact fields kept in the public registers — tells us in advance which data points (services authorised, agents, branches) will be machine-extractable for actor mapping.

source_name: Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (Закон за платежни услуги и платни системи, consolidated text PDF)
why_relevant: The PSD2/EMD2-aligned statute (Off. Gazette 90/2022, in force 2023) that created the licensed non-bank payments layer. Defines the service categories (PIS, AIS, acquiring, remittance, e-money) that map one-to-one onto distinct technology procurement needs.

source_name: NBRSM — Macedonian payment infrastructure overview (Македонска платежна инфраструктура)
why_relevant: Maps the systems layer — MIPS (RTGS), KIBS clearing, CaSys card clearing — and thereby names the infrastructure operators that themselves buy switching, HSM, settlement and connectivity technology. English mirror exists.

source_name: NBRSM oversight page for CaSys card clearing
why_relevant: Regulator's own description of CaSys as an overseen clearing/netting operator — independent confirmation of role, scope and participants, useful to validate corporate claims and to enumerate participating banks/PSPs.

source_name: BIS CPMI Red Book — Payment, clearing and settlement systems in Macedonia
why_relevant: Independent, structured description of MIPS, KIBS and CaSys, their ownership, participants and technical arrangements. Best single English baseline for understanding who operates what before reading MK-language sources; dated but structurally reliable.

source_name: Monri Payments Macedonia (monri.mk) — PSP / online payment gateway
why_relevant: Regional PSP/gateway operating in MK for online card acceptance; a direct competitor/partner in e-commerce acquiring and a buyer of gateway, tokenisation and fraud technology. Its merchant and bank partner pages reveal the acquiring value chain.

source_name: Pari.com.mk — fintech/licensing coverage (Paysera Macedonia first licensed EMI)
why_relevant: Business-press reporting names licensees and their launch plans faster than registers are updated, and often mentions the technology partner or platform behind a launch — the closest thing to visible procurement in a market where private PSPs publish no tenders.

source_name: MKD.mk — fintech coverage (Flex Pay e-money licence)
why_relevant: Documents a second EMI licensee (Флекс пеј), confirming a widening licensed layer. Mainstream media items are the earliest public trace of a new payments buyer entering the market.

source_name: Central Register of North Macedonia (Централен регистар, crm.com.mk)
why_relevant: Company registry feeding ESJN operator data; the way to resolve a licensed PSP/EMI trade name into a legal entity, ownership, capital and annual accounts — needed to size these actors as buyers and to link award notices to register entries.

source_name: Meta.mk — policy reporting on e-money bylaws
why_relevant: Explains, in accessible mk, when the NBRSM bylaws opened the market and what new services became possible — a dating anchor for the licensing timeline and a source of quotes from the regulator on expected market entry.

source_name: Bank Western Union / MoneyGram agent pages (Stopanska, Komercijalna, Sparkasse, TTK)
why_relevant: Remittance in MK is still distributed through bank agent networks rather than standalone licensed remitters. These pages map which global remittance network is tied to which local agent — i.e. who owns the counter technology and where a non-bank remittance licensee would have to displace an incumbent.

source_name: SeeNews — regional business wire (N. Macedonia payments items)
why_relevant: English-language regional wire that reports scheme-processor mandates (e.g. CaSys taking Diners Club processing) — exactly the contract-award-shaped events that never appear in a public tender portal for private payments actors.

source_name: Licentium — North Macedonia licensing hub (commercial advisory)
why_relevant: Advisory-firm summaries of the MK PI/EMI regime (capital, fees, NBRNM process) give a fast English orientation and, importantly, indicate advisory demand — a proxy for how many applicants are in the pipeline. Commercially motivated, so verify against NBRSM.
